name: Delirium Tremens (Alcohol Withdrawal)

matching.reasoningTemplate: Agitation, autonomic hyperactivity, tremor and altered sensorium 48-96 h after the last drink in a heavy drinker suggest delirium tremens - but CNS infection and Wernicke's must be excluded in parallel in any febrile or altered patient.

redFlags: Do NOT anchor on withdrawal in a febrile/altered patient - exclude meningitis/encephalitis (LP) and give thiamine before glucose (Wernicke)
Autonomic storm - hyperthermia, arrhythmia; DT carries appreciable mortality if untreated

investigations.test: Bedside glucose + IV thiamine before glucose (Wernicke prophylaxis)
Exclude CNS infection / structural cause (LP, imaging) when febrile, focal or atypical
Electrolytes incl. Mg/PO4, LFTs; assess CIWA-Ar

references: Harrison 22e - Alcohol and Alcohol Use Disorders
provenanceNote: Recall Tier-4 new diagnosable entity (alcohol withdrawal). AI-drafted matching signature; PENDING clinician sign-off. Intentionally does NOT dominate CNS-infection candidates in a febrile/altered patient - designed to enter the top-3 as a co-consideration.
